as_told.title: Priest of Sais tells Solon about cyclic cataclysm

plain: This is the ancient source of the Atlantis legend, a story of a great island civilisation that was destroyed. A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, says that Solon, a lawmaker of ancient Athens, travelled to Egypt and visited a temple of the goddess Neith at a city called Sais, in the Nile Delta. Hancock says the Egyptian priests there read the picture writing on the temple walls to Solon and translated it for him. He says this is why the Greek philosopher Plato, writing in his works Timaeus and Critias, gives such an early date for Atlantis, around 9600 BC, with Solon's visit around 600 BC. Hancock tells this on two different podcast episodes. Another guest, Tim Alberino, also refers to the priest of Sais teaching Solon. Alberino focuses on the priest's lesson that the world goes through repeated great disasters, and ties it to our own time. If the account is true, an advanced civilisation was lost long before written history.
